items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: I made some...made some numbers over at...over in Paris with Slam Stewart... We played over there.

ctx.x: Is that when he was workin' with Slim Gaillard?

Slim Gaillard was workin' with him. Him an' Slam Stewart was together. So, I played there for a coupla years, an' I took off, went back to New York, played again the Apollo Theater, back up in Washington again, played some nightclubs up there, then I left an' come back to New York again.

And then I...me an' Pete Johnson, Albert Ammons, Meade Lux Lewis...we got together an' we run in...we got a bookin' in Chicago at the Panther Room. In the Panther Room, they had Harry James' band and Frank Sinatra, so we worked with them for about a month.

items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: I've made quite a few recordings with, like you said, Milt Buckner, Jo Jones and Big Joe Turner, the blues singer.

ctx.x: How did you find leading that band?

Well, we went over there more or less to make recordings and go on tour, you know, which we did make quite a few recordings. As of late, you know, as far back as 1972, I've made quite a few recordings with, like you said, Milt Buckner, Jo Jones and Big Joe Turner, the blues singer.
Oh, he worked with you all too?

items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: We had a cat called "The Fiddler." He played the violin. He was good.

ctx.x: Count Basie an' them's band was downtown at a nightclub, an' we was on the other side of town...colored joint. So, when they got off from work, they come out there where we was workin' at, but we stayed open later'n they did. And we'd have a jam session. Ever'body sit in and have a jam session.

We had a cat called "The Fiddler." He played the violin. He was good. But some white boy come through there, played the violin, so we had a contest. White boy outplayed "The Fiddler." He really did. So, we used to have a lot of fun like that. Different cats come in from outa town, like, uh, Stepin Fetchit, Ina Ray Hutton...mmmmn, they come to town, they work downtown at the hotels, so when they get off from work, they come out South where we worked at, so's that's how come we get a chance to meet all those…
We had...Benny Goodman came in...used to get his whole band.
